# Contact martingales give global parameter optimality and rigidity

This is a bounded structural theorem for the attained concave-parameter
route. It proves that the existing volume martingale is already a GLOBAL
certificate for the parameter problem, including arbitrary changes of its
affine pieces. Additional parameter-only first variations therefore cannot
improve a pair carrying this certificate. The theorem supplies no body
deformation and no Gamma payment.

Independent full audit by Defect: PASS, saved in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.
Two-sided has independently full-read the theorem and supplied a second
strictness proof using uniform own-fiber strip bounds, saved in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)` (PASS).

## 1. Abstract actual-measure setting

Let C be a compact convex subset of a finite-dimensional real affine space.
Let m be a finite nonzero Borel measure supported on C, with M=m(C). In the
application this is the actual mixed volume, a finite sum of d-volume on
the positive sampled convex fibers. Let L:C->(0,infinity) be continuous and
concave, normalized by

    (1/M) integral log L dm=0.

Let Y_i belong to C, let sigma_i>0 sum to one, and set L_i=L(Y_i). Suppose
there is a finite-source martingale with source masses sigma_i/L_i and
target dm/(M L). More explicitly, suppose probability laws rho_i on C
satisfy

    E_(rho_i) w=Y_i,
    E_(rho_i) L=L_i,
    sum_i (sigma_i/L_i) rho_i=dm/(M L).                 (1)

The second identity follows from concavity and equality of total L moments
in the audited full-space transport theorem. It is stated explicitly here.
Define the original-volume row laws

    d bar_rho_i=(L/L_i) d rho_i.

They are probabilities, and

    sum_i sigma_i bar_rho_i=dm/M.                      (2)

No row is assumed uniform, supported on an entire fiber, or supported on a
convex set. The actual row barycenter in (1), rather than the barycenter of
bar_rho_i, is used below.

## 2. A global multiplicative inequality

For EVERY positive continuous concave U on C,

    sum_i sigma_i log[U(Y_i)/L_i]
        >=(1/M) integral log[U/L] dm.                  (3)

Proof. Set R=U/L, R_i=U(Y_i)/L_i. Row concavity of U gives

    E_(bar_rho_i) R=E_(rho_i) U/L_i<=R_i.

Since R has a positive lower bound and finite upper bound, all displayed
integrals and logarithms are finite. Jensen for the strictly concave log
then gives

    E_(bar_rho_i) log R
       <=log E_(bar_rho_i) R<=log R_i.

Multiply by sigma_i and sum, using (2). This proves (3) directly, without
interchanging an extremum and integral or differentiating a moving cell.

In particular, if U is also logarithmically normalized, then

    product_i [U(Y_i)/L_i]^(sigma_i)>=1.               (4)

Thus at least one positively weighted old mark has U(Y_i)>=L_i. This
conclusion holds for a finite displacement U, not just an infinitesimal
parameter direction.

## 3. Exact deficit and equality

Put b_i=E_(bar_rho_i) R>0, and define the probability law tau_i by

    d tau_i=(R/b_i) d bar_rho_i.

All these laws are mutually absolutely continuous, with bounded density
ratios. Their relative entropy is

    KL(bar_rho_i || tau_i)
         =log b_i-E_(bar_rho_i) log R.

Consequently the exact gap in (3) is

    sum_i sigma_i { log[R_i/b_i]
                       + KL(bar_rho_i || tau_i) }.     (5)

Both terms inside every brace are nonnegative. Equality holds if and only
if, for every positive row, BOTH

    E_(rho_i) U=U(Y_i),
    U/L=R_i rho_i-almost everywhere.                  (6)

Indeed zero entropy says R=b_i almost surely, and the other zero gap says
b_i=R_i. Conversely (6) sets both gaps to zero. Equality of Jensen for U
alone would not imply this ratio rigidity.

An especially useful uniqueness statement needs no connectedness of row
supports. If U is normalized and U(Y_i)<=L_i for every positive row, the
left side of (3) is nonpositive while the right side is zero. Hence each
U(Y_i)=L_i, equality holds in (3), and (6) gives U=L on every row. By (2),

    U=L m-almost everywhere.                          (7)

In the mixed-volume application, continuity and positivity of volume on
every nonempty relative-open part of each full-dimensional fiber upgrade
(7) to equality on every sampled fiber, including its boundary. There is
no assertion about different concave extensions between sampled fibers.

Equivalently, L is the unique sampled restriction maximizing

    U -> (1/M) integral log U dm

among positive continuous concave U with U(Y_i)<=L_i at every positive
source. The maximum is zero. The constraint set is convex, and the
functional is strictly concave modulo m-almost-everywhere equality; (3)
supplies the actual attained maximizing certificate, rather than an
unproved existence argument for this auxiliary optimization problem.

## 4. Equivalence with the complete radial first-variation dual

For completeness the certificate is not weaker than the parameter
first-order condition used to obtain it. Let

    T_L={h continuous on C: h+cL is concave for some c>=0}.

From (1), Jensen applied rowwise to h+cL gives

    sum_i (sigma_i/L_i)h(Y_i)
        >=(1/M) integral h/L dm                       (8)

for every h in T_L. The cL terms cancel exactly. Conversely the full-space
transport theorem proves that (8), with nonnegative sigma summing to one,
implies the martingale (1): affine tests give full first moments, negative
convex tests give convex order, and the finite-source allocation proof
constructs the coupling; total L-moment equality gives its row contacts.
Those steps are proved in
`candidate 3b257d8ddacb6167`.

Thus the attained parameter first-order dual and this contact martingale
are equivalent. Equation (3) is an additional GLOBAL consequence of the
same dual, not an untested strengthening of its hypotheses.

It also covers changing the affine pieces of a finite-plane L. If

    L_t=min_r(A_r+t B_r)

is positive for small t, it is concave regardless of switches of active
planes. Apply (3) directly to its normalized version. One does not need a
uniform derivative of L_t/t on a crease. Alternatively each exact secant
(L_t-L)/t belongs to T_L for t>0, so (8) already tests every such secant.
No omitted moving-plane condition can overturn this certificate.

## 5. Consequence for actual fixed-body buffered depth

Use the audited fixed-body buffer

    f_U(z,X)=[U(z,X) E_(K_z)(X)/M]^(1/(d+1)).

Assume every Y_i is an actual proper deepest mark for L, with common raw
buffered depth Q and strictly greater pure-base depth. For any other
positive normalized concave U, (4) supplies a mark with U(Y_i)>=L_i.
All its buffered halfspaces then only increase as the buffer increases.
Its depth for U is at least Q. Therefore L is a GLOBAL fixed-body parameter
minimizer of the actual maximum depth.

The global minimizer is unique on the sampled fibers. Here is the precise
strictness input. At a fixed mark of depth Q strictly below its pure-base
depth, increasing the scalar buffer strictly increases its depth. If the
new depth reaches pure-base depth this is immediate. Otherwise the audited
proper-gap attainment lemma supplies an attained new minimizing halfspace
with nonzero continuous normal and a proper own-fiber trace. Reducing that
buffer to its old value raises the threshold by a positive amount and
strictly removes positive own-fiber volume. The old depth is thus strictly
less than the new one. This contradiction proves strictness even when
minimizing directions switch; it does not use one fixed active cut for the
new minimization. Closed halfspaces cause no problem: the proper trace's
boundary has zero d-volume, and the removed positive-width strip has
positive d-volume.

If U has maximum depth no greater than Q, this strictness gives
U(Y_i)<=L_i for all positive source rows. Section 3 then gives U=L on S.
This uniqueness is for fixed bodies, fixed epsilon, and the fixed actual
mass and covariance normalization. It does not compare different bodies.

## 6. Strategic limitation

The exact one-gradient calibration on the ten bases of 3 Delta_2 already
carries a contact martingale and has class depth strictly below Gamma_1
times its total mass, even though it satisfies all strict proper-minor
quotas. The present theorem applies to it and strengthens its parameter
certificate; it cannot remove its class-payment obstruction.

In particular, this theorem closes a possible methodological loophole:
higher-order, finite, moving-crease, or alternative affine-plane changes of
the concave weight cannot lower the depth of a fixed family carrying the
certificate. Further progress on the attained-minimum route has to use
actual body geometry or a different global construction. No implication
to OC is asserted.
